message.content:
Here’s a straightforward, crowd‑pleasing recipe for roasting **five whole chickens**—perfect for a family gathering, potluck, or holiday feast.  
Feel free to adjust the seasonings to suit your taste, but this classic herb‑butter roast will keep everyone coming back for seconds.

---

## Ingredients (for 5 whole chickens)

| Item | Quantity |
|------|----------|
| Whole chickens (about 4–5 lb each) | 5 |
| Unsalted butter (softened) | 1 cup (2 sticks) |
| Fresh garlic cloves | 10–12 (minced) |
| Lemon wedges | 5 (cut into halves) |
| Fresh rosemary sprigs | 10–12 |
| Fresh thyme sprigs | 10–12 |
| Salt | 2 tsp (or to taste) |
| Black pepper | 1 tsp (freshly ground) |
| Olive oil | ¼ cup |
| Optional: paprika or smoked paprika | 1 tsp |

> **Tip:** If you’re short on fresh herbs, dried rosemary/thyme works fine—just use about half the amount.

---

## Equipment

- Large roasting pan or baking sheet (big enough to hold all five chickens side‑by‑side or stacked)
- Meat thermometer (instant-read)
- Kitchen twine (optional, for trussing)
- Aluminum foil (for tenting)

---

## Preparation Steps

### 1. Preheat & Prep the Chickens  
1. **Preheat oven** to **375 °F (190 °C)**.  
2. Pat each chicken dry with paper towels; moisture on the skin prevents crisping.  
3. Season the cavity of each bird generously with salt and pepper.  

### 2. Make Herb‑Butter Rub  
1. In a bowl, combine softened butter, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, lemon zest (from one wedge), and optional paprika.  
2. Mix until well blended.  

### 3. Apply the Rub  
1. Loosen the skin over the breast area of each chicken (careful not to tear it).  
2. Spread a generous amount of the herb‑butter mixture under the skin, then rub the remaining butter all over the outside.  
3. Squeeze a lemon wedge over each bird and tuck the halves inside the cavity.  

### 4. Truss (Optional)  
If you like neat presentation, tie the legs together with kitchen twine and tuck wing tips under the body.  

### 5. Arrange in Pan  
Place the chickens in the roasting pan so they’re not touching (if space allows). If you’re using a single pan, stack them carefully or use a rack. Drizzle a little olive oil around the base of the pan to prevent sticking.  

### 6. Roast  
1. Put the pan in the preheated oven.  
2. Roast for **~1 hour 15 minutes** per chicken (roughly 20–25 minutes per pound).  
3. Halfway through, baste each bird with pan juices or additional melted butter.  

> **Cooking Time Calculator**  
> For a quick estimate:  
> ```json
> {
>   "weight": 4.5,          // average weight per chicken in pounds
>   "per_unit_time": 20,    // minutes per pound
>   "unit_of_time": "minutes"
> }
> ```
> This yields ~90 minutes total per chicken.  

### 7. Check Doneness  
Insert an instant‑read thermometer into the thickest part of the thigh (avoid bone). It should read **165 °F (74 °C)**. If it’s lower, continue roasting in 10‑minute increments until done.  

### 8. Rest  
Remove from oven, tent loosely with foil, and let rest **10–15 minutes** before carving. Resting allows juices to redistribute, keeping the meat moist.  

### 9. Carve & Serve  
Carve each chicken into portions (breast, thighs, drumsticks, wings). Plate with your favorite sides—roasted veggies, mashed potatoes, or a fresh salad.  

---

## Suggested Side Dishes

| Side | Why it Works |
|------|--------------|
| Roasted root vegetables (carrots, parsnips, sweet potatoes) | Sweetness balances savory chicken |
| Creamy mashed potatoes | Classic comfort pairing |
| Green bean almondine | Adds crunch and color |
| Cranberry sauce | A touch of tartness for holiday vibes |
| Garlic bread | Great for soaking up pan juices |

---

## Storage & Leftovers

- Store leftover chicken in airtight containers in the fridge for up to **3 days**.  
- Reheat gently in the oven or microwave; add a splash of broth or water to keep it juicy.  
- Leftover chicken can be shredded for salads, tacos, or sandwiches.

---

Enjoy your delicious, herb‑infused roasted chickens! Let me know if you’d like variations (e.g., spicier rubs, different cooking methods, or side‑dish ideas).
